controls.statement: The fixture runner does not call a setuid or sudo path. It is not a user namespace.
The fixture child receives PATH, language, and Python flags only. Provider credentials are not copied.
Read-only mounts for verified artifacts require a namespace or container. The Python path hook is not that mount.
Read-only candidate configuration requires a namespace or container. This profile does not create one.
The fixture runner uses a temporary working directory. That directory is not a private mount.
The open hook rejects lexical corpus paths. Hiding gold labels from the operating system requires a namespace or container.
The open hook rejects known result file names. Hiding prior results at the operating-system boundary is not implemented.
Path parts named patchpilot or neural-from-scratch are denied lexically. A mount that hides those trees is not implemented.
The child environment omits HOME. The process can still open a home path unless a namespace hides it.
SSH configuration is not copied into the child environment. Hiding the files requires a namespace or container.
Cloud credential variables are not copied. Credential files remain readable without a filesystem namespace.
The socket hook is in-process. It is not a network namespace, seccomp filter, or firewall.
RLIMIT_NPROC can be set on a child. It is a per-user limit, not a private process namespace.
RLIMIT_CPU can stop a child that exceeds its CPU-second budget.
RLIMIT_AS limits address space. It is not resident-set size and it is not a cgroup memory controller.
The fixture runner enforces a 15-second wall clock. Real-candidate ceilings are recorded here and are not applied to fixtures.
RLIMIT_FSIZE can stop a child from writing past the selected file-size budget.
RLIMIT_NOFILE can stop a child from opening files past the selected descriptor budget.
The fixture runner sends SIGKILL to the child process group when the platform permits. It is not a pid namespace.
The fixture runner starts the child with an argument array and shell set to false.
The harness does not raise privileges. It does not prove that the operating system would deny a privileged helper.
The fixture child working directory is the temporary runtime directory chosen by the runner.
The child receives one canonical JSON request on standard input and returns one JSON response on standard output.
